weight.description: Relative flex weight of this component inside a Row or Column. Only meaningful as a direct child of one.

DataQuery.description: A server-side table query applied to dataUri: the table-query request body (POST /v1/artifacts/{id}/table-query) without format. The server runs filter, then aggregate, then downsample, then sort, then offset/limit. Omit columns to request every column of dataUri — except alongside aggregate, where columns is required, since aggregate's output columns (e.g. price_mean) don't exist in the source and so cannot be inferred. limit bounds the rows in ONE response (a transfer size), not the underlying data; offset pages through a larger result across several requests. When a chart or map query would otherwise exceed limit without an explicit downsample, the server instead samples evenly across the full range and reports that it did, rather than silently truncating to the first rows. limit's own maximum here is a generous safety ceiling, not the deployment's real per-response cap, which is server-configured. A viewer (e.g. an interactive data-table) may layer its own user-driven paging/filtering/sorting on top of this dataQuery without replacing it — the agent's own filter/aggregate/downsample intent still applies underneath. Shared verbatim by clio.chart.v1, clio.map.v1, and clio.data-table.v1.

GeoJsonGeometry.description: A GeoJSON Geometry object (RFC 7946 §3.1), strictly shaped: Point/MultiPoint/LineString/MultiLineString/Polygon/MultiPolygon carry coordinates; GeometryCollection carries geometries. Never a Feature/FeatureCollection, never a bare coordinate array.

detail.description: Instruction that stays true at any scale. State fixed per-unit amounts here when needed; do not repeat the starting total or count.

quantity.description: Amount for the guide's baseAmount; the viewer rescales it with the control.

quantityUnit.description: Unit beside the scaled amount at quantity 1; use a singular countable label.

quantityUnitPlural.description: Optional label at other quantities, such as eggs or tubes; omit for invariant units.

category.description: Nominal group, such as station type. Use value for measured numbers.

value.description: Optional measured magnitude for a continuous colour scale and legend.

QueryAggregate.description: Group rows by groupBy (empty or omitted: one global group) and reduce; each metric becomes a result column named {column}_{fn}, which must not repeat a groupBy column.

QueryDownsample.description: How the server thins rows before limit applies. none keeps every row; stride keeps evenly spaced rows (per entityColumn up to maxPerEntity when set, else overall up to limit); per_entity_lttb runs LTTB on (x, y) per entityColumn (the whole table is one series without it) and needs x and y.

QueryFilter.description: One predicate; all filter entries are AND-ed. eq: value is a non-null scalar. in: value is a non-empty list of scalars. range: value is [min, max], inclusive, either side may be null. isnull: value omitted or true matches nulls, false matches non-nulls. contains: value is a non-empty string, matched as a case-insensitive substring of a string column (a per-column text filter).

QuerySort.description: One dataQuery.sort key; earlier entries in the list sort first.

SelectionState.description: The value at a bound selection path (/selection/<key>): the selected values of one data field. source is the id of the component that made the selection.

SpecDataNamedSource.description: Every `data` key anywhere in a Vega-Lite spec is absent or exactly {"name": "source"} — rows come from the component's data/dataUri, never the spec.

SpecNoBindElement.description: No `element` key inside any `bind` object (params[].bind.element) anywhere in a Vega-Lite spec, at any depth — it is a CSS selector that could mount a Vega input widget into any element on the host page, not just this chart.

SpecNoForbiddenKeys.description: No `url` or `usermeta` key anywhere in a Vega-Lite spec, at any depth.

time.description: ISO 8601 local date-time with an explicit UTC offset or Z.

action.description: What clicking this node does, such as an openView call for the view of the branch it stands for.

agentDisplayName.description: Text to be displayed next to the surface to identify the agent or tool that created it.

iconUrl.description: A URL for an image that identifies the agent or tool associated with the surface.

primaryColor.description: The primary brand color used for highlights (e.g., primary buttons, active borders). Renderers may generate variants of this color for different contexts. Format: Hexadecimal code (e.g., '#00BFFF').

Button.description: A clickable control wrapping one child, firing an action.

Carousel.description: Browse child views one at a time, such as images, captioned instructions, or video.

ChoicePicker.description: A single- or multiple-selection picker; bind value to the path an action reads.

Column.description: A vertical layout container for child components.

DateTimeInput.description: A date, time, or date-time input with an ISO 8601 value; enable the needed parts.

Divider.description: A horizontal or vertical rule separating layout regions.

Frame.description: A titled container around one child component.

Grid.description: A fixed-column grid layout container for child components.

Icon.description: A named or SVG icon glyph.

Image.description: A raster or vector image by URL, sized to a preset variant.

List.description: A vertical or horizontal list of child components, optionally templated from bound data.

Modal.description: A dialog opened by a trigger component, showing one content component.

Row.description: A horizontal layout container for child components.

Slider.description: A whole-number range control (see clio.slider.v1 for fractional steps).

Tabs.description: A tabbed switcher between named child components.

Text.description: A run of text, plain or headed (h1-h5, caption, body).

TextField.description: A single- or multi-line text input.

Video.description: A video from a registered file, with playback and full-screen controls.

clio.action-card.v1.description: A short pitch with up to six labeled actions.

clio.approval.v1.description: A gated decision with one to four actions.

clio.artifact.v1.description: A reference card for one registered artifact.

clio.callout.v1.description: A short flagged note distinct from plain text (info/warning/error severity).

data.description: Inline rows (at most 10000) — this array rides the surface's own wire message, so it is capped for transfer size; for a larger or growing dataset use dataUri instead, unbounded and paged/downsampled by the viewer. A cell is a scalar OR a strictly-shaped GeoJSON Geometry object ($defs/GeoJsonGeometry), so a geoshape mark can draw real shapes from inline rows.

dataUri.description: A workspace file path or artifact:// reference; CLIO registers a path as an artifact before validation. Or a live study source, study://<study>/measurements, study://<study>/entries or study://<study>/records/<view>, which updates as the study records entries.

selection.description: Bind to /selection/<key>; the bound value is a SelectionState ({field, values[], source?}, see $defs/SelectionState). Components bound to the same path share one selection.

selectionField.description: Column used for an explicit selection binding. Ordinary views of one dataUri link by __row without this property; trajectory and spectra points select exact rows while entityField groups each curve.

spec.description: A Vega-Lite spec whose rows come from data/dataUri as the named dataset 'source' — the spec is chart configuration, never a data channel, and the dataset itself is unbounded via dataUri regardless of this cap. This schema already enforces the top-level key allowlist, no url/usermeta key at any depth, no bind.element at any depth (a CSS selector that could mount an input widget anywhere on the host page), and data only as {name: source} at any depth; the renderer additionally enforces the config-size (65536 bytes) and view-count (8) caps that keep the spec itself bounded and abuse-resistant, which JSON Schema cannot express. See a2ui/chart/guard_rules.json.

allOf.description: Exactly one of spec or preset; preset fill fields need preset.
Exactly one of data or dataUri is required.
Fields used by the trajectories preset.
Fields used by the heatmap preset.
Fields used by the spectra preset.
Fields used by the boxplot preset.
Fields used by the scatter preset.

clio.chart.v1.description: Any chart over tabular rows: a preset or an Altair/Vega-Lite spec.

code.description: Inline source; use dataUri instead for a referenced file.

dataUri.description: A workspace file path or artifact:// reference; CLIO registers a path as an artifact before validation. Its file content is the source.

allOf.description: Exactly one of code or dataUri is required.

clio.code.v1.description: Syntax-highlighted source, inline or from a referenced file.

columns.description: Required with inline rows; optional with dataUri (defaults to the queried/dataset columns).

dataUri.description: A workspace file path or artifact:// reference; CLIO registers a path as an artifact before validation. Or a live study source, study://<study>/measurements, study://<study>/entries or study://<study>/records/<view>, which updates as the study records entries.

pageSize.description: Rows per page at first (default 10); the reader can change it.

rows.description: Inline rows; use dataUri instead for a registered dataset.

selection.description: Bind to /selection/<key>; the bound value is a SelectionState ({field, values[], source?}, see $defs/SelectionState). Components bound to the same path share one selection.

selectionField.description: Dataset column the shared selection's values are drawn from; required when selection is bound.

allOf.description: Exactly one of rows or dataUri is required.
columns is required alongside inline rows.
selectionField is required when selection is bound (an object, not a literal).

clio.data-table.v1.description: Tabular rows, inline or from a referenced dataset.

dataUri.description: A workspace file path or artifact:// reference; CLIO registers a path as an artifact before validation. Its file content is the diff text.

diff.description: Inline unified diff text; use dataUri instead for a referenced file.

allOf.description: Exactly one of diff or dataUri is required.

clio.diff.v1.description: A unified diff for one path, inline or from a referenced file.

camera.description: Camera literal or data-model binding. longitude/latitude/zoom are required; bearing and pitch default to zero. Bound cameras are shared and updated by human navigation. Use update_a2ui_data_model on the declared path to pan, zoom or rotate, then capture the resulting view.

categoryField.description: Dataset column grouping points into categories.

dataUri.description: A workspace file path or artifact:// reference; CLIO registers a path as an artifact before validation. Or a live study source, study://<study>/measurements, study://<study>/entries or study://<study>/records/<view>, which updates as the study records entries. Requires latitudeField/longitudeField/labelField; a referenced dataset is bounded by dataQuery/limit, not the inline point cap.

detailField.description: Dataset column holding each point's detail text.

filterFields.description: With dataUri, columns worth filtering while exploring this map. Choose one or more real columns from the task and dataset, such as a category, magnitude, or time column. Use a registered table even for small maps when these native filters matter. The viewer creates typed controls and applies them to the map and Reference this; omit for the viewer's default fields.

geojsonUri.description: Artifact URI of a GeoJSON FeatureCollection. Geometry is read by reference and drawn as points, lines, and polygons; feature properties supply labelField, categoryField, or valueField when named.

idField.description: Dataset column holding each point's stable id.

labelField.description: Dataset column holding each point's label (required with dataUri).

latitudeField.description: Dataset column holding latitude (required with dataUri).

longitudeField.description: Dataset column holding longitude (required with dataUri).

orderField.description: With trackField, time or numeric sequence column ordering positions along each trajectory.

points.description: Inline points (at most 500) — this array rides the surface's own wire message, so it is capped for transfer size; for a larger dataset use dataUri instead, unbounded and paged/downsampled by the viewer.

selection.description: Bind to /selection/<key>; the bound value is a SelectionState ({field, values[], source?}, see $defs/SelectionState). Components bound to the same path share one selection.

selectionField.description: Dataset column the shared selection's values are drawn from; required when selection is bound.

trackField.description: With dataUri, column identifying each trajectory (for example storm_id). Rows with the same value form one path.

valueField.description: Numeric dataset column used for a continuous colour scale and legend.

valueLabel.description: Human-readable name for the numeric map legend, such as Displacement.

valueUnit.description: Unit shown beside a continuous-colour legend's values.

allOf.description: Exactly one of points, dataUri, or geojsonUri is required.
dataUri requires the point field names.
selectionField is required when selection is bound (an object, not a literal).

clio.map.v1.description: Interactive points, ordered trajectories, or GeoJSON geometry on a map.

source.description: Inline diagram source; use dataUri instead for a referenced file.

clio.mermaid.v1.description: Mermaid diagrams: workflows, protocols, ER/class models, states, git histories, grammars, trees and 33 supported families. Load this component for syntax and examples.

families.example:
flowchart LR
  raw[Raw input] --> check{Valid?}
  check -->|Yes| save[Save]
  check -->|No| repair[Repair]
  repair --> check
families.syntax: LR/RL/TB/BT set direction. id[Label], id{Decision}, --> edges, -->|condition| labelled edges; subgraph id[Label] ... end groups nodes. Stable IDs differ from display labels. classDef/class can mark semantic categories.

families.example:
sequenceDiagram
  actor Reader
  participant API
  Reader->>API: Request
  alt Allowed
    API-->>Reader: Record
  else Denied
    API-->>Reader: Error
  end
families.syntax: actor/participant name lifelines; ->> sends and -->> replies. alt condition / else condition / end is exclusive; opt, loop, par and critical blocks also end with end. activate/deactivate and Note over are available. A request and reply are separate messages.

families.example:
classDiagram
  class Sensor {
    +string id
    +read()
  }
  class Recorder
  Recorder "1" o-- "1..*" Sensor : reads
families.syntax: class Name { type field; method() } uses one member per line. <|-- inheritance, *-- composition, o-- aggregation, --> association; quoted multiplicities precede relation ends. + public, - private.

families.example:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Idle
  Idle --> Running : start
  Running --> Failed : error
  Failed --> Running : retry
  Running --> Complete : success
  Complete --> [*]
families.syntax: [*] is entry/exit; A --> B : trigger. state Label as ID gives aliases. Composite state ID { ... } nests transitions; <<choice>>, <<fork>>, <<join>> express branching. Do not confuse states with actions.

Entity { type name PK/FK } lists attributes. || exactly one, o| zero or one, }o/o{ zero or many, }|/|{ one or many. -- identifying, .. non-identifying; read the marker at each entity end independently. If an attribute type is not supplied, use an unspecified placeholder and explain it. Do not infer primary/foreign keys from names or add attributes to make an entity box look complete. Retain unknowns as unknowns.

families.example:
gantt
  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
  section Trial
  Collect :a, 2026-10-01, 2d
  Analyse :b, after a, 3d
families.syntax: dateFormat controls input dates; section groups rows. Task :id,start,duration; after id starts after a dependency. done, active, crit and milestone are task tags. Use real dates/durations or label them illustrative.

families.example:
gitGraph
  commit id: "A"
  branch trial
  commit id: "B"
  checkout main
  commit id: "C"
  merge trial id: "M"
families.syntax: commit id: "label" creates a commit on the active branch. branch name creates/switches a branch; checkout name switches; merge name merges it into the active branch. cherry-pick id: copies a commit; tag/type are commit options. Preserve branching points, not just labels.
families.use: Commit ancestry, branch histories and merges.

families.example:
mindmap
  root((Study))
    Inputs
      Samples
      Metadata
    Outputs
      Report
families.syntax: Indentation determines parent/child structure. root((Label)) is a root shape; children may use [rectangle], (rounded), {{hexagon}}. Equal indentation means siblings; do not use it for message order.

families.example:
timeline
  title Trial history
  2025 : Pilot
  2026 : Replication : Review
families.syntax: title names the view; section groups periods. Period : event : another event associates events with a period. A following : event extends it.

families.example:
journey
  title Review experience
  section Evidence
    Find source: 3: Analyst
    Inspect result: 5: Analyst, Reviewer
families.syntax: section groups stages. Task: score: Actor, OtherActor gives a 1–5 experience score and responsible actors. Scores are not measured timings.

families.example:
pie title Synthetic allocation
  "Analysis" : 60
  "Review" : 40
families.syntax: pie title ... followed by "Category" : numericValue; showData shows values. Keep original units and denominators clear; use charts for linked data.

families.example:
quadrantChart
  x-axis Low effort --> High effort
  y-axis Low value --> High value
  quadrant-1 Plan
  quadrant-2 Prioritise
  quadrant-3 Defer
  quadrant-4 Reconsider
  Trial: [0.3, 0.8]
families.syntax: x-axis Low --> High and y-axis Low --> High label axes; quadrant-1..4 label regions. Item: [x,y] places a point with coordinates in [0,1].
families.use: Items positioned on two qualitative axes.

families.example:
xychart-beta
  x-axis [A, B, C]
  y-axis "Count" 0 --> 10
  bar [3, 7, 5]
families.syntax: x-axis [categories] or a numeric range; y-axis title min --> max; bar [values] and line [values]. Array positions must match x values.

requirement ID { id: ...; text: ...; risk: low/medium/high; verifymethod: test/analysis/inspection/demonstration } uses separate lines. element ID { type: ... } names evidence/system elements. A - satisfies -> B (also verifies, traces, refines, contains, copies, derives).

families.example:
sankey-beta
Input,Accepted,8
Input,Rejected,2
Accepted,Report,8
families.syntax: After the declaration, CSV rows are source,target,value. Quote names containing commas. Edge width represents the numeric value; use consistent units.

families.example:
architecture-beta
  group lab(cloud)[Lab]
  service api(server)[API] in lab
  service db(database)[Store] in lab
  api:R -- L:db
families.syntax: group id(icon)[Label]; service id(icon)[Label] in groupId. Built-in icons include cloud, database, disk, server, internet. a:R -- L:b connects right/left ports; :T/:B top/bottom; arrows add direction. These symbols are not connections to real services.

families.example:
C4Context
  Person(reader, "Reader")
  System(catalog, "Catalog")
  Rel(reader, catalog, "Finds evidence")
families.syntax: Person(id,"Label"), System(id,"Label"), Container(id,"Label","Tech"), Component(id,"Label","Tech"), Rel(a,b,"Purpose"). Boundaries use braces. C4Dynamic uses ordered Rel calls; Deployment_Node contains Container instances. Do not mix context systems with deployment nodes without explaining the level.
families.use: Architecture at a declared level of abstraction.

families.example:
block-beta
  columns 2
  a["Acquire"] b["Analyse"]
  c["Review"]:2
  a --> c
  b --> c
families.syntax: columns N sets columns; id[Label]:span spans columns; space reserves a cell. block:group ... end nests blocks; A --> B adds relationships. Use this when explicit grouping matters more than automatic graph layout.

families.example:
packet-beta
  0-3: "Version"
  4-7: "Flags"
  8-15: "Length"
families.syntax: start-end: "Field" assigns an inclusive bit range; +N: "Field" appends N bits. Preserve field widths and ordering. It does not model message exchanges.

families.example:
kanban
  todo[To do]
    clean[Clean samples]
  done[Done]
    collect[Collect samples]
families.syntax: ColumnID[Column label] at one indent, cardID[Card label] beneath it. Card metadata can set assigned, ticket and priority. It illustrates state; it does not create CLIO tasks or make cards a live task board.

families.example:
radar-beta
  axis q["Quality"], s["Speed"], c["Coverage"]
  curve a["Trial A"]{8, 4, 6}
  max 10
families.syntax: axis id1["Label"], id2["Label"]; curve series["Label"]{values}; max N sets the scale. Values follow axis order. Do not invent normalized scores.

families.example:
treemap-beta
  "Work"
    "Analysis": 6
    "Review": 4
families.syntax: Indent "Group" headings and "Leaf": value children. Area represents the numeric weight, not temporal order; preserve the hierarchy and units.

Choose one notation. EBNF: name = expression ;, quoted terminals, bare rule references, adjacency sequence, | choice, [x] optional, (x) grouping, x* zero-or-more, x+ one-or-more. ABNF: name = expression, / choice, [x] optional, *x zero-or-more, 1*x one-or-more, %x41 hex terminal. ABNF quoted literals are case-insensitive; for exact ASCII case use %x byte sequences, e.g. %x4F.50.45.4E for OPEN. This pinned renderer does not accept RFC 7405 %s/%i prefixes. EBNF/PEG quoted literals are case-sensitive; identical displayed labels do not prove language equivalence. PEG: name <- expression ;, / ordered choice, x? optional, x* and x+ repetition, &x/!x lookahead; quote terminals. End productions with ; in each notation in this renderer. The railroad DSL uses name = terminal("word") ; with nonterminal("rule"), sequence(...), choice(...), optional(...), zeroOrMore(...) and oneOrMore(...). Do not mix operators; define referenced rules and preserve optionality.
families.use: Accepted token sequences in a grammar.

families.syntax: Flowchart-like direction, nodes and edges, with semantic shapes @{ type: input/tool/action/refdoc/decision/task }. --> is sequence; reference/failure links have different meaning. This is a diagram, not an agent execution or task submission mechanism.
families.use: Agent actions, tools, inputs and reference documents.

families.example:
treeView-beta
  study/
    data/
      readings.csv
    report.md
families.syntax: Indent children beneath parents; a trailing / denotes a directory. A file has no trailing /. ## description annotates an entry. Preserve names/extensions; displaying a file does not grant/open it.

families.example:
cynefin-beta
  complex
    "Explore hypothesis"
  clear
    "Apply checklist"
families.syntax: complex/complicated/clear/chaotic/confusion headings with indented "Item" labels. domain --> domain : label marks a transition. Domains express the decision context, not measured risk scores.
families.use: Classify decisions by the Cynefin domains.

families.example:
wardley-beta
  anchor Reader [0.95, 0.5]
  component Report [0.8, 0.6]
  component Storage [0.2, 0.85]
  Reader -> Report
  Report -> Storage
families.syntax: anchor Name [visibility,evolution]; component Name [visibility,evolution]; A -> B is a dependency; evolve Name target proposes evolution. Coordinates are in [0,1]; label hypothetical positions as estimates.

families.example:
eventmodeling
  tf 01 ui ReviewUI
  tf 02 cmd SubmitReview
  tf 03 evt ReviewSubmitted
  tf 04 rmo ReviewList
families.syntax: tf frame kind Name defines a frame; kinds ui, cmd, evt, rmo, pcr identify user interface, command, event, read model, processor. [[dataName]] references a data block. Frame order is chronology, not a generic causal arrow between arbitrary nodes.
families.use: Commands, events and read models over chronological frames.

families.example:
usecase-beta
  actor reader("Reader")
  inspect("Inspect evidence")
  reader --> inspect
families.syntax: actor id("Label"), goal("Label"); systemBoundary id[Label] ... end groups goals. actor --> goal associates them. include/extend relate use cases; inheritance is different from a sequential workflow.
families.use: Actors and goals within a system boundary.

families.example:
venn-beta
  set A[Reviewed]:8
  set B[Published]:6
  union A,B:3
families.syntax: set A[Label]:size; set B[Label]:size; union A,B:overlap describes an intersection. Use consistent counts and feasible intersections, not arbitrary decorative circle sizes.

families.example:
ishikawa-beta
  Missing records
    Inputs
      Late arrival
      Invalid format
families.syntax: An effect heading and indented category/cause hierarchy forms the fishbone. Categories group hypotheses, not proven causation. Keep evidence-backed causes distinguishable from suggestions.

families.example:
swimlane-beta LR
  subgraph analyst[Analyst]
    submit[Submit]
  end
  subgraph reviewer[Reviewer]
    inspect[Inspect]
  end
  submit --> inspect
families.syntax: LR or TB selects direction; subgraph actor[Actor] ... end creates a lane; ordinary flowchart nodes/arrows connect actions across lanes. Lane ownership is distinct from a sequence diagram lifeline.

families.example: info
families.syntax: The declaration alone renders version/diagnostic information. Use only when diagnosing the viewer, not as a diagram of user data.

host: Use source OR dataUri, never both. dataUri uses the actual returned artifact URI of a registered UTF-8 source file. Where the producer accepts a workspace file path, it registers that file before validation; reuse its returned URI. Do not guess artifact IDs or use HTTP URLs. source can be a dynamic string binding; the bound value is diagram text.

Render requested diagrams with the declared A2UI surface tools, including inline chat explanations. A mermaid fenced block displays source code, not a rendered visual; use it when the user asks for source or Markdown export. If rendering is unavailable, report the limitation. Use the declared dashboard tools for a saved composed report. Do not install Pele, import JavaScript, or invent clio.pele.v1.

CLIO supplies theme colours and adaptive container width. Renderer options maxWidth, responsive, config, themeVariables and custom CSS are not component properties. Mermaid init directives, HTML labels, arbitrary callbacks and external images/links are rejected. Text line breaks use literal backslash-n inside labels (encoded as \\n in JSON); source statements use JSON \n.

Navigation: add a standalone flowchart line: click data "workspace-folder:data/inputs" "Open inputs". data must be an existing node; the relative directory must exist in the current workspace. Encode reserved path characters. The host opens Files using existing access. This does not run code, create a folder, or grant permissions. Plain exports do not provide workspace navigation.

The component has source view, zoom, pan, expand, copy, SVG/PNG/source export and selection/reference controls supplied by the viewer. Do not add fake toolbar properties. Tree filenames, architecture services and git commits are diagram text; they do not automatically become file navigation.

Preserve semantics before styling: branch conditions, message order, entity cardinality, grammar repetition and hierarchy are different relationships. Use clio.chart.v1 for data-backed quantitative views needing units, filters or shared selection; Mermaid chart families remain available for small self-contained illustrations. Use graph views for exploratory node networks.

Review the actual published artifact: inspect its captured image at the docked width and expanded when useful, including titles, text, arrows and legends. Fix clipping, tiny text, lost edges or misleading relationships and capture again. A valid schema, accepted source or SVG is not a visual pass. If capture is unavailable, report that specific gap. The shared review-visual-presentation skill supplies the capture workflow.

On an error, repair the actual declaration, quoting, indentation, block endings or operators; preserve difficult relationships. CLIO can fall back to Mermaid for legacy syntax, but Pele-only declarations need Pele. Do not silently replace the diagram with an unrelated gallery. External Mermaid plugins such as ZenUML and custom icon resolvers are not exposed.

notation_variants.C4Component:
C4Component
  Component(api, "API", "HTTP")
  Component(store, "Repository", "Python")
  Rel(api, store, "Reads records")

C4Container
  Person(reader, "Reader")
  Container(api, "API", "Python")
  ContainerDb(db, "Records", "SQL")

  Rel(api, db, "Reads")

C4Dynamic
  Person(reader, "Reader")
  Container(api, "API", "HTTP")
  Rel(reader, api, "Requests record")

references.version_rule: This inventory follows the pinned consumer, not the latest website. New library versions require a fresh coverage and rendering check.

x-clio-authoring.scope: Complete family inventory for CLIO's bundled Pele 1.6.0. These are source declarations inside the existing Mermaid component, not component names. Each family has a working starting example and its authoring operators. The examples are synthetic, not measurements. Adapt relationships and labels to the actual evidence; there is no required diagram or panel set.

component_example.source:
flowchart LR
  input[Input] --> check{Valid?}
  check -->|Yes| save[Save]
  check -->|No| repair[Repair]
component_example.title: Review decision

source_encoding.rule: The source value contains actual line breaks between statements. JSON encodes each newline once as \n. Do not double-escape them as \\n, which leaves backslash and n characters in the source. When writing JSON from Python/JavaScript, construct a multiline source string and serialize the document once. Label-internal backslash-n is a different syntax.

clio.mesh-viewport.v1.description: An orbitable 3D view of a registered standard mesh or a CLIO FEA mesh with optional result fields.

clio.message-draft.v1.description: Editable alternatives for an email, chat message, or text, with copy and open actions.

clio.metric.v1.description: One labeled number, optionally with a unit and trend.

clio.progress.v1.description: A bounded or indeterminate operation's progress.

clio.raster-viewport.v1.description: An interactive viewport for a registered two-dimensional grid, with sampled values, colour scale, and region reference.

clio.slider.v1.description: A fractional-step numeric control, or a two-value range, with typed value boxes.

clio.status.v1.description: A single labeled state, e.g. a running step.

clio.steps.v1.description: An interactive protocol or recipe with checkable actions, timers, and separately scaled ingredients.

observedAt.description: ISO 8601 local date-time with an explicit UTC offset or Z.

clio.weather.v1.description: Current weather and hourly or daily forecasts for a field site or location.

dataUri.description: A workspace file path or artifact:// reference; CLIO registers a path as an artifact before validation. A JSON file shaped {"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]}.

nodes.description: Inline nodes (at most 128) — rides the surface's own wire message; give edges too, or use dataUri instead of both for a larger graph, unbounded.

selected.description: The selected node id; bind it to follow a selection.

allOf.description: Exactly one of nodes+edges or dataUri is required.

clio.workflow.v1.description: A step/edge graph showing a multi-step plan's progress.

description: CLIO scientific-agent A2UI components, including interactive data views and widgets.

and.description: Performs a logical AND operation on a list of boolean values.

values.description: The list of boolean values to evaluate.

email.description: Checks that the value is a valid email address.

focusWorkflow.description: Focuses one node of a clio.workflow.v1 component.

stepId.description: The workflow node id to focus.

formatCurrency.description: Formats a number as a currency string.

decimals.description: Optional. The number of decimal places to show. Defaults to 0 or 2 depending on locale.

grouping.description: Optional. If true, uses locale-specific grouping separators (e.g. '1,000'). If false, returns raw digits (e.g. '1000'). Defaults to true.

formatDate.description: Formats a timestamp into a string using a pattern.

format.description:
A Unicode TR35 date pattern string.

Token Reference:
- Year: 'yy' (26), 'yyyy' (2026)
- Month: 'M' (1), 'MM' (01), 'MMM' (Jan), 'MMMM' (January)
- Day: 'd' (1), 'dd' (01), 'E' (Tue), 'EEEE' (Tuesday)
- Hour (12h): 'h' (1-12), 'hh' (01-12) - requires 'a' for AM/PM
- Hour (24h): 'H' (0-23), 'HH' (00-23) - Military Time
- Minute: 'mm' (00-59)
- Second: 'ss' (00-59)
- Period: 'a' (AM/PM)

Examples:
- 'MMM dd, yyyy' -> 'Jan 16, 2026'
- 'HH:mm' -> '14:30' (Military)
- 'h:mm a' -> '2:30 PM'
- 'EEEE, d MMMM' -> 'Friday, 16 January'

formatNumber.description: Formats a number with the specified grouping and decimal precision.

decimals.description: Optional. The number of decimal places to show. Defaults to 0 or 2 depending on locale.

grouping.description: Optional. If true, uses locale-specific grouping separators (e.g. '1,000'). If false, returns raw digits (e.g. '1000'). Defaults to true.

formatString.description: Performs string interpolation of data model values and other functions in the catalog functions list and returns the resulting string. The value string can contain interpolated expressions in the `${expression}` format. Supported expression types include: JSON Pointer paths to the data model (e.g., `${/absolute/path}` or `${relative/path}`), and client-side function calls (e.g., `${now()}`). Function arguments must be named (e.g., `${formatDate(value:${/currentDate}, format:'MM-dd')}`). To include a literal `${` sequence, escape it as `\${`.

not.description: Performs a logical NOT operation on a boolean value.

openArtifact.description: Opens a registered artifact in the workspace artifact viewer.

uri.description: The artifact:// or resource:// URI to open.

openUrl.description: Opens the specified URL in a browser or handler. This function has no return value.

openView.description: Opens a study view or a dashboard, optionally with a selection applied.

selection.description: A selection to apply in the opened view, at /selection/<key>.

key.description: The selection's key: it is written at /selection/<key> (not a `path`, which A2UI reads as a data binding).

view.description: A study view's entry id (e_...) or a dashboard's artifact:// URI, from any conversation of this workspace.

or.description: Performs a logical OR operation on a list of boolean values.

values.description: The list of boolean values to evaluate.

pluralize.description: Returns a localized string based on the Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR) plural category of the count (zero, one, two, few, many, other). Requires an 'other' fallback. For English, just use 'one' and 'other'.

few.description: String for the 'few' category (e.g., small groups in Slavic languages).

many.description: String for the 'many' category (e.g., large groups in various languages).

other.description: The default/fallback string (used for general plural cases).

two.description: String for the 'two' category (used in Arabic, Welsh, etc.).

value.description: The numeric value used to determine the plural category.

regex.description: Checks that the value matches a regular expression string.

pattern.description: The regex pattern to match against.

required.description: Checks that the value is not null, undefined, or empty.

selectData.description: Writes a selection to the data model: a SelectionState {field, values: rowIds, source: 'selectData'} at path. Every component whose selection is bound to that path follows it.

field.description: The data field the row identifiers are values of.

path.description: The data-model path the selection is written to, /selection/<key>: the same path the linked components bind their selection to.

rowIds.description: The selected row identifiers; written as the values.

surfaceId.description: The surface the selection applies to; defaults to the current surface.
